summary:
Recommendation: make Manifold (elalish/manifold, Apache-2.0, v3.5.4 released 2026-09-25) the primary geometry kernel for openBrick, and keep OpenCascade OCCT 8.0.x (LGPL-2.1 with exception) as an optional, out-of-process fallback used only for true parametric fillets and STEP export. Manifold is a mesh-based CSG kernel whose booleans are guaranteed to produce manifold (watertight) output, which is exactly the property a 3D-print pipeline needs; it is the engine Blender 4.5 LTS (July 2025) and OpenSCAD nightlies (default since 2025-08-17) adopted, it has first-party WASM/TypeScript (manifold-3d, 541 KB wasm / 204 KB gzip measured), Python (manifold3d 3.5.4) and C bindings, and since 3.5.0 (May 2026) it produces bit-identical results across architectures, which lets openBrick hash and cache community parts deterministically. For Rust there are two live routes: manifold-csg 0.4.1 (safe FFI over the C++ library, Apache-2.0/MIT, 2026-09-09) and manifold-rust 0.19.1 (a pure-Rust port of Manifold 3.5.0 sponsored by MatterHackers, 2026-10-25, 33 stars but all 730 upstream tests ported). A pure-Rust kernel removes the C++ toolchain from mobile and WASM builds entirely, so the suggested architecture is a Rust core behind a small kernel trait with manifold-rust as default and manifold-csg as the hedge; a TypeScript client would use manifold-3d directly.

Fillets, text and SVG are all handled with Manifold plus a 2D layer, not with 3D fillet operations. Brick geometry does not need a B-rep fillet: stud-top chamfers are a frustum cap (Cylinder with two radii, or Extrude with scaleTop) or a revolved 2D profile that already contains the chamfer arc; comfortable vertical edges on tiles, nameplates and keychains come from Clipper2 round offsets (inset-then-outset) on the CrossSection before extrusion; top/bottom edge rounding is available three ways in increasing cost: Extrude scaleTop chamfer (free, and better for FDM overhangs anyway), SmoothOut + RefineToTolerance (cosmetic small fillets), and MinkowskiSum with a low-poly sphere (exact rounding, added in 3.4.0, slow, run as a budgeted background job). An SDF route (Manifold::LevelSet over a smooth-min SDF) gives perfect fillets for organic merch shapes without taking a dependency on fidget or libfive. Text is font outline -> shaping (harfrust/rustybuzz in Rust, opentype.js 2.0 in JS, fontTools in Python) -> Bezier flattening (kurbo) -> CrossSection with NonZero fill -> Extrude, then union (emboss) or subtract (engrave). SVG is usvg 0.49 -> flattened paths with the file's fill rule -> CrossSection -> Extrude; stroke-to-outline via lyon or Clipper2 open-path offsetting is a v1.1 item.

STEP export is the one thing a mesh kernel cannot do well. The clean answer is a parametric 'recipe' intermediate representation for parts (the same thing the UI edits) that compiles to Manifold for interactive/print use and to OCCT for STEP and true fillets when asked. The Python route (build123d 0.13.0 on cadquery-ocp 8.0.1.1.0) is mature and fine for desktop/CLI/CI; the Rust route is cadrum 0.9.1 (MIT wrapper, prebuilt OCCT 8.0.1, native + wasm32 via Docker, has fillet/chamfer/STEP) or occt-wasm 5.1.0 (OCCT 8 inside wasmtime, 4.7 MB compressed, ~2x native). Do not build on opencascade.js (last npm release 2023-03-23, wraps OCCT 7.6.2, 48.9 MB wasm / 9.1 MB brotli), and keep OCCT off iOS where LGPL static-link relinking obligations bite. Rejects: CGAL (algorithms are GPL, incompatible with an MIT-distributed app without a GeometryFactory licence), OpenSCAD as an embedded kernel (GPL-2.0; fine as an isolated import/export sandbox, its 2026.10.25 WASM web build is only 3.35 MB), Fornjot (archived 2026-06-19), opencascade-rs (WIP, LGPL), csgrs (BSP-based 0.20.1 on crates.io; an unpublished 0.23 rewrite claims certified booleans, watch it), three-bvh-csg (experimental, not guaranteed manifold, its README points to Manifold), JSCAD (MIT, V3 still alpha 3.0.7-alpha.0, own engine; useful as API inspiration only), and GPU SDF meshing libraries (sdf2mesh 0.1.0, last commit Jan 2025) which are not ready to plan around.

findings.claim: Manifold's latest release is v3.5.4 (2026-09-25); 3.5.x shipped cross-platform determinism, ray casting, boolean progress/cancellation (ExecutionContext) and a WASM CSP fix; 3.4.0 (2026-02/03) added MinkowskiSum/MinkowskiDifference and removed MeshIO from the public API.
findings.evidence: GitHub releases page lists v3.5.4 (25 Sep), v3.5.0 (23 May, determinism, ExecutionContext), v3.4.0 (27 Feb, Minkowski, MeshIO removal); npm 'time' field confirms 3.4.0 published 2026-03-14, 3.5.0 2026-05-23, 3.5.4 2026-09-25.

findings.claim: Manifold is Apache-2.0, guarantees manifold output from booleans, supports vertex properties, Smooth/Refine, LevelSet (SDF) meshing, and has C, WASM/JS (manifold-3d), Python (manifold3d), Rust (manifold-csg, manifold-rust), Java, C#, Julia, OCaml, Swift and Clojure bindings; WASM builds are serial-only and parallel WASM is 'not recommended'.
findings.evidence: README: 'primary goal is reliability: guaranteed manifold output without caveats or edge cases'; bindings list; 2.4k stars; note that parallel WASM may cause memory corruption.

findings.claim: The manifold-3d 3.5.4 npm package ships a 541,470-byte manifold.wasm (203,834 bytes gzip -9) plus an 82 KB manifold.js glue file; the 1.73 MB worker.bundled.js is the ManifoldCAD worker and is not needed by the core.
findings.evidence: Measured locally on 2026-10-27 with npm pack manifold-3d@3.5.4, tar extraction and gzip -9; package.json license Apache-2.0.

findings.claim: Manifold has no fillet/chamfer operation; edge rounding is achieved via SmoothOut (minSharpAngle default 52.5 deg, minSmoothness > 0 gives 'a small fillet on these sharp edges') + RefineToTolerance, via MinkowskiSum (dilation, cost grows with the product of face counts), via Extrude scaleTop/Cylinder with two radii for chamfers, or via LevelSet over an SDF.
findings.evidence: Manifold C++ class docs describe Smooth, SmoothOut, RefineToTolerance, MinkowskiSum/Difference, Extrude (scaleTop, {0,0} forms a cone), Cylinder(circularSegments, two radii), LevelSet (marching tetrahedra on body-centred grid); fillets/chamfers are not documented as operations.

findings.claim: Manifold's 2D CrossSection is built on Clipper2 (Boost Software License 1.0) and provides boolean union by default, fill rules, offsetting (round joins) and extrude(height, nDivisions, twist, scaleTop); this is the mechanism for rounded corners, print calibration offsets and font/SVG polygon ingestion.
findings.evidence: manifold-3d CrossSection docs: constructor takes closed contours + fill rule, 'uses the Clipper2 library for polygon clipping (boolean) and offsetting'; Clipper2 repo lists BSL-1.0, 2.5k stars, intersection/union/difference/XOR plus offsetting.

findings.claim: manifold-csg 0.4.1 (2026-09-09, Apache-2.0 OR MIT, zmerlynn) is a safe Rust binding over C++ Manifold covering booleans, CrossSection + Clipper2 offset, extrude/revolve, hull, Minkowski, refine/smooth, LevelSet, warp, f64 MeshGL64; it builds Manifold from source (git+cmake+C++) or links a prebuilt install; wasm32-unknown-emscripten is tested, wasm32-unknown-unknown is 'provisional' (needs LLVM 20+, exceptions abort); mobile is not mentioned.
findings.evidence: docs.rs crate page for manifold-csg 0.4.1; manifold3d 0.4.1 on crates.io is a facade that re-exports manifold-csg.

findings.claim: manifold-rust 0.19.1 (2026-10-25, Apache-2.0, Lars Brubaker, sponsored by MatterHackers) is a pure-Rust port of Manifold v3.5.0 claiming all 18 engine phases and all upstream tests ported (730 passing in release), performance within a few percent of sequential C++ (sphere-sphere 2M tris 2.57 s vs 2.61 s), an optional rayon 'parallel' feature (native only, bit-identical), a WASM demo, a C FFI and a second 'robust' boolean engine; it has only 33 stars and performance/corpus claims are self-reported.
findings.evidence: docs.rs and GitHub README; release history 0.9.0 (July 2026) to 0.19.1; documented divergences in docs/CPP_DIVERGENCES.md; Thingi10K sweep with 0 NotClosed failures; 120 s Cancelled budget on heavily self-intersecting meshes.

findings.claim: manifold3d 3.5.4 is on PyPI (Python 3.14 wheels since 3.4.1); trimesh 5.2.0, cadquery-ocp 8.0.1.1.0, build123d 0.13.0 and cadquery 2.8.0 are the current PyPI versions.
findings.evidence: pip index versions run on the dev box on 2026-10-27; Manifold 3.4.1 release notes mention Python 3.14 wheel builds.

findings.claim: OCCT 8.0.0 was released 2026-05-07 (C++17 baseline, BRepGraph, stream-based thread-safe STEP I/O with ~20% smaller files, ARM64 on macOS/Windows, VTK off by default) and 8.0.1 followed on 2026-07-30; OCCT is LGPL-2.1 with the OCCT_LGPL_EXCEPTION or a commercial licence; 3.1k stars.
findings.evidence: occt3d.com 8.0.0 release post; Wikipedia version table lists 8.0.1 / 30 July 2026; GitHub README states LGPL-2.1 with exception file and commercial alternative.

findings.claim: OCCT's official build guide covers Windows (VS2019+/MinGW), Linux (GCC 8+/Clang 7+), macOS (Xcode 11+), Android (NDK r19+, API 21+, cross-compile walkthrough) and WebAssembly (Emscripten SDK 3.0+, listed only in system requirements); iOS is not covered on that page.
findings.evidence: OCCT 'Building OCCT' documentation page (redirected to occt3d.com).

findings.claim: OCCT's BRepFilletAPI_MakeFillet has long-standing robustness issues: failures when the radius exceeds adjacent edge length, IsDone()==true with visibly wrong geometry, sensitivity to model scale/units and to construction history, and ordering-dependent workarounds; most tracker entries are still open.
findings.evidence: OCCT Mantis tracker issues 28596, 33849, 30208, 31229, 31764, 26778, 27007, 22727 and a FreeCAD tracker thread describe these cases.

findings.claim: opencascade.js is stale: last npm release 1.1.1 on 2023-03-23 (beta tags up to 2023-03-23), README wraps OCCT 7.6.2, LGPL-2.1, 942 stars; its full build is 48.9 MB wasm (9.1 MB brotli) and a custom build is 7.1 MB (2.4 MB compressed), with -sDISABLE_EXCEPTION_CATCHING=1 cutting ~45%.
findings.evidence: npm view opencascade.js time (2026-10-27); GitHub README badge; ocjs.org file-size page.

findings.claim: cadrum 0.9.1 (2026-10-21, MIT wrapper over prebuilt headless OCCT 8.0.1, LGPL-2.1 for OCCT) offers booleans, fillet_edges, chamfer_edges, sweeps/lofts, STEP read/write, BRep, STL/glb/SVG/PNG export, prebuilt binaries for x86_64/aarch64 Linux, x86_64 Windows, x86_64/aarch64 macOS, and wasm32-unknown-unknown via a wasi-sdk Docker image; docs say distributors must let end users relink OCCT; only 42% documented; Android/iOS not mentioned.
findings.evidence: docs.rs cadrum page.

findings.claim: occt-wasm 5.1.0 (2026-10-25, MIT/Apache wrapper, embedded OCCT V8 binary LGPL-2.1-only) runs OCCT inside wasmtime with no C++ toolchain: fuse/cut/common, fillet, chamfer, shell, offset, draft, sweeps/lofts, STEP/STL import-export, glTF export, 170+ methods; 4.7 MB compressed / 21-22 MB loaded, 128 MiB linear memory, compute within ~2x of native; not for browsers (separate npm package).
findings.evidence: docs.rs occt-wasm page.

findings.claim: opencascade-rs (bschwind) is LGPL-2.1, 271 stars, 'a major work in progress' maintained in spare time; fillets, chamfers, STEP and STL are listed as goals, WASM is not available; occt-sys 7.8.1 and the opencascade crate 0.3.0 are its published pieces.
findings.evidence: GitHub README; cargo search on 2026-10-27.

findings.claim: truck (ricosjp) is an actively maintained Apache-2.0 Rust B-rep/NURBS kernel (1.7k stars, commits through 2026-10-26 including STEP conic output fixes) with truck-shapeops 0.4.0 (booleans on solids), truck-stepio 0.3.0 (STEP read/write) and truck-js; no fillet support is documented.
findings.evidence: GitHub repo and commits page; cargo search versions.

findings.claim: Fornjot was archived by its owner on 2026-06-19 with a notice that the project has been shut down and its goals were never reached.
findings.evidence: GitHub repository banner reported in search results.

findings.claim: csgrs on crates.io is 0.20.1 (2025-07-24, MIT), a BSP-tree CSG library (CSG.js translation) with TrueType/Hershey text, 2D offset, SDF meshing, STL/DXF, WASM feature and fillets only on the roadmap; the GitHub README now references an unpublished 0.23.0 (Rust 1.95+) built on a 'Hypermesh' crate claiming certified solid booleans with exact predicates, SVG import and more export formats.
findings.evidence: docs.rs csgrs 0.20.1 page; cargo search returns 0.20.1; GitHub README quick start cites 0.23.0 and 11,392 commits.

findings.claim: OpenSCAD's Manifold backend became the default in development snapshots on 2025-08-17 (CGAL still selectable via --backend=cgal); the last stable release on the GitHub releases page is still 2021.01; nightlies are at 2026.10.25 with WebAssembly web/node packages (web zip 3,353,867 bytes, node zip 4,717,697 bytes); OpenSCAD is GPL-2.0 (COPYING 'Version 2, June 1991' with a CGAL linking exception).
findings.evidence: OpenSCAD mailing-list announcement; GitHub releases page shows 2021.01 as Latest; files.openscad.org/snapshots listing; COPYING file.

findings.claim: openscad-wasm (GPL-2.0, 432 stars) is a full headless port of OpenSCAD to an ES6 WASM module that passes --enable=manifold; openscad-playground moved to the openscad GitHub organisation and defaults to Manifold.
findings.evidence: openscad-wasm README; openscad-playground repository.

findings.claim: Blender 4.5 LTS (July 2025) added a 'Manifold' boolean solver based on the Manifold library in both the Boolean modifier and Geometry Nodes; it only works on manifold meshes.
findings.evidence: Blender 4.5 manual Boolean Modifier page and all3dp coverage.

findings.claim: CGAL is dual-licensed: kernel/support libraries LGPL-3+, most algorithms (including mesh booleans) GPL-3+, commercial licences via GeometryFactory; CGAL 6.2 (2026-06-11) split Polygon Mesh Processing into packages including a dedicated 'Boolean Operations On Meshes' package; 6.2.1 shipped 2026-09-04.
findings.evidence: cgal.org license page; GitHub releases page.

findings.claim: JSCAD (MIT, 3.3k stars) publishes @jscad/modeling 2.13.0 (stable, 2026-02 added Minkowski) and V3 alphas up to 3.0.7-alpha.0 (2026-08-02); V3 uses its own geometry engine (no Manifold mention) and is volunteer maintained.
findings.evidence: npm view @jscad/modeling time; JSCAD forum V3 alpha posts; GitHub README.

findings.claim: three-bvh-csg 0.0.18 (2026-02-17) remains 'experimental, in progress'; input must be watertight and output 'may not be correctly completely two-manifold'; its README points to Manifold for robust CAD-style operations.
findings.evidence: npm view three-bvh-csg time; README.

findings.claim: fidget 0.5.1 (2026-09-27, MPL-2.0, 510 stars) is a 'personal-scale experimental project' with JIT on x86_64/aarch64 (interpreter on wasm32), Manifold Dual Contouring meshing 'much less battle-tested than libfive', an optional fidget-wgpu crate, and a maintainer who tells serious users to 'expect to fork it'.
findings.evidence: docs.rs fidget 0.5.1 page; GitHub README.

findings.claim: libfive core, stdlib and Python bindings are MPL-2.0 (Studio and Guile bindings GPL-2+), 1.7k stars; recent commits (Oct 2026) are Qt 6.11/MSVC/Eigen 5 build fixes rather than feature work.
findings.evidence: GitHub README and commits page.

findings.claim: GPU SDF meshing has no production-ready library: sdf2mesh is 0.1.0 with last commit January 2025; other hits are demos, forum WIPs and a Blender add-on.
findings.evidence: docs.rs sdf2mesh; Codeberg repo; Babylon.js forum threads.

findings.claim: The 2D/font/SVG toolchain for a Rust core is current: usvg 0.49.0, ttf-parser 0.25.1, harfrust 0.15.0, rustybuzz 0.20.1, kurbo 0.13.1, lyon 1.0.19; for JS, opentype.js 2.0.0 shipped 2026-05-06 and fontkit 2.0.4 is available.
findings.evidence: cargo search and npm view run on the dev box 2026-10-27.

findings.claim: A mesh kernel is sufficient for brick-compatible parts: stud chamfers, tube walls, tile edges and keychain loops are all extrude/revolve/offset constructions, so true B-rep fillets are only needed for engineering STEP handoff, not for printable brick geometry.
findings.evidence: Inference from Manifold's Extrude(scaleTop), Cylinder(two radii), Revolve and CrossSection offset capabilities versus the LEGO-style feature set in the README/brief.

findings.claim: Shipping OCCT inside an iOS app is a licensing hazard: LGPL-2.1 static linking requires letting users relink, which cadrum's own docs flag; keep OCCT desktop/server-side or dynamically linked.
findings.evidence: cadrum docs state distributors must comply with LGPL 2.1 and end users must be able to rebuild and relink OCCT; OCCT README lists LGPL-2.1 with exception.

findings.claim: Manifold 3.5.0's cross-platform determinism makes content-addressed caching and reproducible community part hashes feasible across desktop, mobile and WASM builds of the same kernel version; manifold-rust additionally documents divergences from C++ output, so mixing the two implementations in one hash space needs its own cross-check harness.
findings.evidence: Manifold 3.5.0 release notes (determinism check in CI); manifold-rust docs/CPP_DIVERGENCES.md.

options_compared.option: Manifold (C++ core; manifold-3d WASM/TS; manifold3d Python)
options_compared.status_2026: v3.5.4 2026-09-25; 2.4k stars; adopted by Blender 4.5 LTS and OpenSCAD nightlies; releases roughly monthly
options_compared.pros: Guaranteed-manifold booleans; tiny WASM (541 KB / 204 KB gzip); TS, Python, C, Swift, C# bindings; CrossSection+Clipper2 offsets; Extrude/Revolve/Hull/Minkowski/LevelSet/Smooth; cross-platform determinism; 3MF/glTF tooling in npm package
options_compared.cons: No B-rep, no parametric fillet/chamfer op, no STEP; Minkowski slow; WASM single-threaded; C++17 toolchain needed for native builds
options_compared.fit_for_openbrick: Primary kernel. Covers assembler, part designer and print pipeline needs; chamfers/roundings via profile, scaleTop, offset, SmoothOut or Minkowski.

options_compared.pros: No C++ toolchain: builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown, iOS/Android Rust targets, CLI from one crate; all upstream tests ported; perf parity with sequential C++; extra 'robust' engine; C FFI
options_compared.cons: Very young and single-maintainer; self-reported benchmarks; documented divergences from C++ output; 50% doc coverage; parallel only native
options_compared.fit_for_openbrick: Default implementation behind a kernel trait for a Rust core; hedge with manifold-csg. Needs an in-house conformance corpus (brick parts + Thingi10K subset).

options_compared.option: manifold-csg / manifold3d (Rust FFI over C++ Manifold)
options_compared.status_2026: 0.4.1 2026-09-09; tracks upstream Manifold; listed in Manifold README
options_compared.pros: Full upstream behaviour and bug fixes; f64 MeshGL64; CrossSection offsets, Minkowski, LevelSet, smooth/refine; emscripten target tested
options_compared.cons: Builds Manifold from source (git, cmake, C++); wasm32-unknown-unknown provisional (LLVM 20+, no exceptions); mobile untested; pre-1.0 API churn with migration guides
options_compared.fit_for_openbrick: Fallback Rust binding; same trait as manifold-rust so either can be swapped per platform.

recommendations: Adopt Manifold 3.5.x as the primary kernel. If the core is Rust (recommended for desktop+mobile+CLI from one codebase), define a small Kernel trait and ship manifold-rust as default with manifold-csg behind a feature flag; if the core is TypeScript, use manifold-3d directly. Pin the kernel version per file-format version so hashes stay reproducible.

Model brick features so no 3D fillet op is needed: studs = Cylinder + frustum chamfer cap (or Revolve of a chamfered profile); tubes/walls = extruded CrossSections; tile/keychain edge comfort = Clipper2 round inset/outset on the 2D profile; bottom-edge chamfers via Extrude scaleTop (prints better than fillets on FDM).

Offer three rounding tiers in the part designer with explicit cost: (1) chamfer (instant), (2) SmoothOut+RefineToTolerance cosmetic fillet (fast), (3) MinkowskiSum with an 8-16 segment sphere (background job with time budget, part size limits). Add an SDF 'organic' mode built on Manifold::LevelSet with smooth-min fillets for logo blobs and keychains.

Text pipeline: bundle OFL fonts; shape with harfrust/rustybuzz (Rust) or opentype.js 2.0 (JS); flatten Beziers with kurbo at a tolerance derived from nozzle width (e.g. 0.05 mm); build CrossSection with NonZero fill; Extrude; union for emboss, subtract for engrave; run a 2D thin-feature check (offset -r then +r) against the printer profile's minimum feature size before export.

SVG pipeline: usvg 0.49 -> flattened subpaths with the SVG fill rule -> CrossSection -> Extrude; v1 supports fills only, strokes via lyon stroke tessellation or Clipper2 open-path offsetting in v1.1; reject or auto-fix self-intersections through CrossSection's union-on-construct.

Make the part definition a parametric recipe IR (JSON) that the UI edits and the kernel compiles. Compile to Manifold for interactive/print output; compile the same recipe to OCCT (build123d in Python for CLI/CI, cadrum or occt-wasm for a Rust binary) only when the user requests STEP or true parametric fillets. This keeps STEP a v2 feature without architectural debt.
Keep OCCT out of the mobile binaries (LGPL relink obligations, size). Mobile and web get Manifold only; STEP export on mobile can be served by a CLI/server job.

Do not link GPL code (OpenSCAD, CGAL) into the MIT app. If .scad interoperability matters to the maker community, run openscad-wasm (3.35 MB) in an isolated worker/process distributed as a separate GPL component.

Standardise tessellation: set Manifold Defaults (circular segments / min angle / min edge) per export profile, use a fixed segment count for studs/tubes (e.g. 48-64 at 4.8 mm stud diameter) so stud-tube booleans are stable, and apply printer calibration as 2D offsets on the CrossSection before extrusion/revolve (stud radius +/- 0.02-0.08 mm per profile).

Build a conformance corpus early: every brick primitive, a few hundred community merch parts, and a Thingi10K subset; run it on manifold-rust, manifold-csg/manifold-3d and (for STEP parts) OCCT in CI, asserting watertightness, volume agreement and hash determinism. This is the insurance policy for the pure-Rust bet.
Export 3MF as the first-class print format (manifold-3d already depends on @jscadui/3mf-export; keep colours/material per mesh), with STL/OBJ/glTF secondary; treat STEP as engineering handoff only.

Watch-list for 2027: manifold-rust maturity and star growth, csgrs 0.23 'certified booleans' publication, truck-stepio as a permissive STEP writer, OCCT 8.x Emscripten builds, OpenSCAD's first stable release since 2021.01.
